Act II: 'The Database Dependency' — zoom in on the data's smoking gun: Fred's share is highest in Database (81.7%) and Service Desk (87.8%), but the Database group is the sharper problem because non-Fred agents have a demonstrably under-developed bench (Luke Wilson has handled only one Database ticket), making it a true single point of failure for a critical system. Contrast this with Network, where Beth Anglin's 36 assignments prove a deeper bench already exists. Highlight June 2023's critical-only spike for Fred as the concrete failure moment of this dependency. Act III: 'The Untapped Capacity' — pivot from fairness to resilience. Argue that the fix is not a generic algorithm but a targeted two-pronged strategy: (1) Immediate rebalancing in Network/Software/Hardware by implementing a simple threshold rule (no agent exceeds 2x the team average) to leverage existing cross-closure capabilities (teammates already close 78% of Fred's tickets at statistically indistinguishable speeds); (2) A deliberate, formalized cross-training and shadowing program focused specifically on Database and Service Desk for Luke Wilson and Beth Anglin, turning their proven ability to close Fred's tickets (but lower self-closure rates) into proactive assignment capacity. Conclude by framing the issue not as Fred's workload, but as the organization's untenable dependency on a single individual for two critical, high-volume categories. Interview IT operations managers to validate the risk of this specific skills gap and the practical feasibility of the cross-training plan.
